title: The value of an option to exchange one asset for another
annotation: Prices the option to exchange one lognormal asset for another in closed form, using the second asset as numeraire.

title: Pricing and hedging spread options
annotation: Surveys the models and numerical methods used to price and hedge spread options.

title: Extreme correlation of international equity markets
annotation: Uses extreme-value theory to show that international equity correlation rises in bear markets but not in bull markets, and is tied to the market trend rather than to volatility.

title: Asymmetric correlations of equity portfolios
annotation: Measures exceedance correlations of US stocks with the market, finds them much larger on the downside, and finds regime-switching models capture the asymmetry better than other models tried.

authors: Hong, Y. and Tu, J. and Zhou, G.
title: Asymmetries in stock returns: statistical tests and economic evaluation
annotation: Gives model-free tests for asymmetric correlations, betas and covariances, and measures their value to an investor.

authors: Fouque, J.-P. and Pun, C. S. and Wong, H. Y.
title: Portfolio optimization with ambiguous correlation and stochastic volatilities
venue: SIAM Journal on Control and Optimization 54(5), 2309-2338
annotation: Solves worst-case portfolio choice over an ambiguous correlation between two assets, with an asymptotic closed form when their volatilities are fast mean-reverting.

authors: Driessen, J. and Maenhout, P. J. and Vilkov, G.
title: The price of correlation risk: evidence from equity options
annotation: Finds that market-wide correlation risk is priced, from S&P 100 index options against options on its components.

authors: Buraschi, A. and Porchia, P. and Trojani, F.
title: Correlation risk and optimal portfolio choice
annotation: Solves intertemporal portfolio choice with a stochastic (Wishart) covariance matrix and finds a distinct hedging demand against correlation risk.

title: Wishart processes
annotation: Introduces the Wishart process, a matrix-valued diffusion later used to model stochastic covariance.

authors: Da Fonseca, J. and Grasselli, M. and Tebaldi, C.
title: Option pricing when correlations are stochastic: an analytical framework
annotation: An analytical framework for option pricing with stochastic correlation, built on Wishart covariance dynamics.

title: Derivative pricing with Wishart multivariate stochastic volatility
venue: Journal of Business and Economic Statistics 28(3), 438-451
annotation: Prices derivatives when the covariance matrix of several assets follows a Wishart process.

title: Multivariate European option pricing in a Markov-modulated Levy framework
venue: Journal of Computational and Applied Mathematics 317, 171-187
annotation: Prices multi-asset European options when the parameters of a Levy model are modulated by a Markov chain.

title: The calculation of cumulants via conditioning
venue: Annals of the Institute of Statistical Mathematics 21(1), 215-218
annotation: Introduces the conditional-cumulant formula used here to organize the exact all-order joint cumulant tensor of the Gaussian occupation-time mixture.

authors: Kovchegov, Y. and Meredith, N. and Nir, E.
title: Occupation times and Bessel densities
annotation: Derives occupation-time distributions for continuous-time Markov chains and explains the modified-Bessel form used in the two-state certificate.

authors: Coolen-Schrijner, P. and van Doorn, E. A.
title: The deviation matrix of a continuous-time Markov chain
venue: Probability in the Engineering and Informational Sciences 16(3), 351-366
annotation: Defines and studies the continuous-time deviation matrix D = integral_0^infinity (P(t)-Pi) dt, the group-inverse object governing the arbitrary-start initial-layer coefficient used here.

authors: van Dijk, N. M. and Sladky, K.
title: On the total reward variance for continuous-time Markov reward chains
annotation: Establishes asymptotically linear variance growth for finite-state continuous-time Markov reward chains and gives formulas for its growth rate; the boundary Hessian here refines the finite-horizon constant term.
